evidence.quote: **Your current list** (optional): step 1 builds on it and step 2 ranks it.
evidence.rationale: An existing prospect sheet is the starting list step 1 adds to and step 2 scores and tiers.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional).
evidence.rationale: The org context can supply buyers, voice and offer facts for the copy foundation step; the run works without it.

evidence.quote: **Your product page text, price and what it replaces** (required).
evidence.rationale: Existing product page copy is read by step 1 as source text for buyer research; it is read, not rewritten.

evidence.quote: **Your offer, with terms and dates** (required).
evidence.rationale: The offer with terms and dates feeds the offer brief and the quiz's buy box and result pages.

evidence.quote: export the answers and the drop-off numbers for each question
evidence.rationale: The quiz tool's drop-off numbers per question are the results data step 3 reads alongside the answers.

evidence.quote: **Your product list and who each product suits** (required for the quiz result pages).
evidence.rationale: The product list and who each suits is the product data the quiz routes buyers to on its result pages.

evidence.quote: **After launch: the exported quiz answers** (one row per person, one column per question)
evidence.rationale: The exported answers sheet, one row per person, is what step 3 counts and ranks angles from; it exists only after launch.

evidence.quote: Step 1 reads it, and step 2 uses it for the product facts.
evidence.rationale: A saved capture of the store's own product page can supply the page text and price that steps 1 and 2 read.

evidence.quote: **Customer words** from reviews, tickets, surveys or calls, with source and date
evidence.rationale: Customer words from reviews and tickets feed the step 1 buyer research and make it better.

evidence.quote: **The brand's facts, voice, products, offers (with effective dates), claims register, personas and look** (optional)
evidence.rationale: The org context gives voice, offers, claims and personas that the chained skills use for the VIP perks, invite and touch scripts; it is optional.

evidence.quote: export, for customers who meet it, their order count, total spend and last order date
evidence.rationale: The customer export for those who meet the VIP rule is what step 2 sizes tiers from and step 3 picks touches from.

evidence.quote: one row per order with customer, date, order value, discount code, refunds, and cost or margin
evidence.rationale: The order history for a closed window is the results sheet the method names; step 1 ranks customers by profit from it.

evidence.quote: **Customer words from reviews, tickets, surveys or calls, with source and date** (optional)
evidence.rationale: Dated customer words from reviews and tickets are optional context for the chained skills when choosing perks and personal touches.

evidence.quote: If your facts are not written down yet, build them first with the Org context builder.
evidence.rationale: The org context is where the written-down product facts and claims come from when the owner has built one; it is optional because pasted notes also work.

evidence.quote: **Rival ads or claims** (optional). Paste two or three.
evidence.rationale: Rival brands' ads or claims let step 1 check which facts rivals already state; without them every claim is marked rivals not checked.

evidence.quote: the product facts and the offer
evidence.rationale: The live offer is handed to the headline writer in step 2 alongside the claims and product facts.

evidence.quote: and the buyer in a line
evidence.rationale: A one-line buyer from the org context's buyers part is what the cover-test ranker in step 3 reads each headline as.

evidence.quote: **Your product facts** (required): what it is, the price, how it is used.
evidence.rationale: The products part gives what it is, price and use, which steps 2 and 4 combine with the claims for headlines and the image ad.

evidence.quote: and product photos** (optional).
evidence.rationale: Product photos let the single image ad planner in step 4 show the real product in its image prompt.

evidence.quote: **Your notes on how the product is made, sourced and tested** (required), in full
evidence.rationale: The full maker, supplier and test notes are the long source step 1 mines for facts rivals never state.

evidence.quote: your buyer and their words
evidence.rationale: Customer words are optional material that describe the buyer in their own language for the headline and cover-test steps.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional).
evidence.rationale: The optional org context can supply the product facts and the guarantee and return terms that the offer and guarantee steps are given.

evidence.quote: **Your sessions and orders** for the current offer and each version (required for step 5)
evidence.rationale: The performance sheet of sessions and orders per offer version feeds the profit-per-session check that picks the winner and trust score.

evidence.quote: one buyer's main doubt in their own words
evidence.rationale: The buyer's main doubt in their own words is the persona input that the offer builder builds the whole offer around.

evidence.quote: **Your costs:** cost per unit, shipping and fulfilment per order, and payment fees (required).
evidence.rationale: Product data gives the product, price and unit, shipping and fee costs that every margin, break-even and profit sum uses.

evidence.quote: and **your org context** (optional).
evidence.rationale: An existing org context can add known buyers and offer facts to the buyer brief and kill check steps. Optional; the run starts from the idea alone.

evidence.quote: Your idea, written as a question
evidence.rationale: The idea, written as a question with who it is for and search words, is what step 1 turns into searches and every later step tests.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional). Step 2 uses it for your voice and offers.
evidence.rationale: The optional org context is passed to marketing-plan-writer in step 2 for voice and offers. Steps 1 and 3 do not need it.

evidence.quote: **Your strategy, goal or plan** as it stands today (required). Messy is fine.
evidence.rationale: The person's question is their current strategy or goal as written, plus business, budget and team. The strategy check in step 1 reads it exactly as given.

evidence.quote: **Ad copy** (required): your current ad's words and offer, for the rules check to compare against.
evidence.rationale: The brand's current ad words and offer are compared with the final script in the step 5 ad rules check.

evidence.quote: **Org context** (required): your org context, or the website it can be built from.
evidence.rationale: The org context grounds the gap map and the script in the brand's own proof and voice.

evidence.quote: **List of competitors** (optional): the three to six competitors that matter to you.
evidence.rationale: The competitor list tells the study board and category map which brands' ads matter and should be confirmed.

evidence.quote: **Product facts** (required): what it is, what's in it, price, and the claims you may and may not make.
evidence.rationale: Product facts limit every claim in the script to what the brand may say, checked at hand-back.

evidence.quote: **Ads you collected from other brands** (required): for each ad, its library ID
evidence.rationale: The saved competitor ads with IDs and screenshots are the reference set step 1 sorts into the study board.

evidence.quote: **Customer reviews** (required): reviews, survey answers or support emails, copied as written.
evidence.rationale: Customer reviews let step 2 test repeated claims against what buyers say and back the script's idea.

evidence.quote: your facts, products, offers with dates, claims you may make, what creators must not say
evidence.rationale: Steps 1 and 2 read the org context for the gifting plan, the card, the claims the creator may make and the script's voice.

evidence.quote: **The footage the creator sends back** (required for step 4, after the pause).
evidence.rationale: The creator's raw clips are what video-ad-edit-planner cuts against the approved script in step 4.

evidence.quote: a close with the approved offer
evidence.rationale: The live offer and its terms supply the close the edit plan ends on. No offer beyond the approved script is added.

evidence.quote: **Who you want to reach**
evidence.rationale: The buyer description guides which creators fit, judged by whether they already post about the buyer's problem. It also guides who the phone-video script speaks to.

evidence.quote: price, variants, how it opens and is used, and what never appears on camera
evidence.rationale: Step 3 passes the product facts to creator-filming-brief-writer, so the brief covers how to show the product and what stays off camera.

evidence.quote: Step 2 builds the script from your buyers' own words.
evidence.rationale: The copied customer reviews give selfie-style-ad-script the buyers' real words for the situation, the snag and the anchor detail.

evidence.quote: **Your org context or your own pages** (optional): step 2 uses them to show which reasons you never say.
evidence.rationale: Step 2 compares buyer reasons with the org context to list the reasons the brand never says.

evidence.quote: **Product facts** (optional): price, variants, how it is used.
evidence.rationale: Product facts help the interview planner frame questions about how the product is bought and used.

evidence.quote: **What you want to learn** (required for step 1): for example why people choose you or why they switch.
evidence.rationale: The user's question sets what the interview plan in step 1 is built to learn.

evidence.quote: **The interview answers** (required for step 2): what customers said, word for word
evidence.rationale: Customer words, interviews plus any reviews and tickets with dates, are what step 2 ranks into buying reasons.

evidence.quote: **Your offer** and **your org context** (optional).
evidence.rationale: The org context's claims and offer facts are what the step 3 launch check compares the price and claims against.

evidence.quote: **Your clips** (required): the file names, each clip's real length and shape
evidence.rationale: The video clips, with real lengths and contents, are what the edit planner times into the cut list.

evidence.quote: the script and your offer and claims
evidence.rationale: The offer's real terms are read by the pre-launch checker to confirm the close and on-screen price match what is sold.

evidence.quote: **Your script** (required): beat by beat, with on-screen text and shots.
evidence.rationale: The video ad script is the only source of words, claims and offer terms for the cut list and word-for-word captions.

evidence.quote: **The exported video** (required, after the pause). It is the input to steps 2 and 3.
evidence.rationale: The exported video ad is what gets captioned in step 2 and checked before launch in step 3.

evidence.quote: products, buyers and claims in one place.
evidence.rationale: The org context gives the products and buyers, which help name the two grid axes in step 1 (who buys and what for).

evidence.quote: revenue and margin for each product over the last 12 months, and the team hours each one takes
evidence.rationale: The product and programme numbers are the results the ranking rule uses (margin earned per team hour) and that the programme review and give-up list cite.

evidence.quote: It needs the decision, each person's view and reason, and the owner.
evidence.rationale: The question is the decision to cut the line, with who argued against each cut and who owns it, which the commit note in step 4 records.

evidence.quote: the thread for each task, with the recipient.
evidence.rationale: The matching email threads, exported or pasted as text, are the documents step 1 matches to each task to find the recipient and context.

evidence.quote: each task with its due date, owner and status, as an export or paste.
evidence.rationale: The due task list, with dates, owners and statuses, is the plan of work that decides which tasks need a follow-up draft.

evidence.quote: **What you are making and where people will meet it** (required): a talk, article, course, product page or song, and the goal.
evidence.rationale: The brief of what is being made, where it is met and its goal is what the two-audience brief writer turns into step 1's brief.

evidence.quote: **Who the experts are and who the newcomers are** (required): real comments from each group if you have them.
evidence.rationale: Personas of the expert and newcomer groups name the two audiences and their needs that every later step writes and tests for.

evidence.quote: **Your results export** (required) for a closed date window, with its definitions.
evidence.rationale: The closed-window ad results export is what step 3 judges every ad set and ad against the target with.

evidence.quote: These are the reference set for step 1.
evidence.rationale: The ads you ran, with win or loss roles, are the reference set step 1 splits into message and look.

evidence.quote: Step 3 uses them to say who the product is not for.
evidence.rationale: The org context or product facts let the buyer profile in step 3 say who the product is not for.

evidence.quote: **A topic, a rival or a product category, and who you think buys it** (required)
evidence.rationale: The person's topic and guessed buyer is the question; it sets the Reddit search terms for step 1 and frames every later step.

evidence.quote: **Funnel numbers for one named period** (required): visits, sign-ups and users still active after 30 days
evidence.rationale: The product or analytics export of visits, sign-ups and 30-day actives for set dates is the results sheet step 1 finds the leak in.

evidence.quote: **A buyer profile** in your customers' own words: their problem, trigger, wants and doubts
evidence.rationale: An optional buyer profile helps pick who to test with and which first-visit change fits their problem and doubts.

evidence.quote: **The new-user goal** (required): what a new user should do, and what a good outcome looks like.
evidence.rationale: The owner's goal for new users and what good looks like is the question the leak report and test plan answer.

evidence.quote: **The page new users land on**, as a link or saved HTML (optional)
evidence.rationale: The link to the landing page gives the usability test a real first-visit page to set tasks on.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional).
evidence.rationale: The optional org context can supply the brand name and variants used to split branded clicks from non-branded clicks in the recovery report.

evidence.quote: **A Search Console export covering the drop and an equal earlier period** (required)
evidence.rationale: The Search Console pages and queries export is the search query report the diagnoser reads to find lost clicks and causes.

evidence.quote: **Crawl or indexing reports, or page screenshots** (optional): they sharpen steps 1 and 2.
evidence.rationale: Page screenshots and crawl or indexing captures of the store sharpen the diagnosis and the ranked fix list.

evidence.quote: **Your Shopify theme files** (needed for step 3 only)
evidence.rationale: The Shopify theme files let the duplicate page fixer write code changes; without them step 3 gives only the plan and settings.

evidence.quote: an org context's offers and claims files help step 1 tell a real tactic from a wish.
evidence.rationale: The org context's offers and claims files help the order checker separate real tactics from wishes, and change the impact and ease scores in step 3.

evidence.quote: **Your marketing plan** (required): the text, in any order or state.
evidence.rationale: The required question port carries the person's marketing plan text and the goal they care about most; step 1 sorts that text and step 3 cuts it to the goal.

evidence.quote: **Rival ads or pages** (optional, three or more is best): step 3 uses them for the swap test.
evidence.rationale: Rival ads are given to the flaw-first writer and the fresh line rewriter. The swap test checks that the chosen line could not run unchanged for a rival.

evidence.quote: **A short description of your typical buyer** (optional): the problem, what triggers them, their doubts and the words they use.
evidence.rationale: The buyer description gives the buyer instinct brief the problem, triggers, doubts and words. The brief uses these to name the drive behind buying and the feeling the ad must leave.

evidence.quote: **Your product facts** (required): what it is, what it does, its price, its proof, and what it does badly.
evidence.rationale: Product facts, including what the product does badly, give the true flaw to lead with. They are also the proof each ad line is checked against.

evidence.quote: **Buyer words** (optional): reviews, support messages, return reasons or survey answers, with source and date.
evidence.rationale: Reviews and return reasons with source and date feed step 1's brief. They show which flaw buyers already see and the words they use for it.

evidence.quote: the brand's facts, voice, products, offers, claims and buyers
evidence.rationale: The org context is what step 1 turns into ten episodes, and its facts and voice keep the script from inventing lines.

evidence.quote: the clips of the founder filming the first episode
evidence.rationale: The video clips are the founder's filmed first episode, which step 4 cuts into an edit plan; without them step 4 stops.

evidence.quote: ten real buyer questions, in the buyers' own words
evidence.rationale: The buyers part of the org context supplies real buyer questions in their own words, which the series planner sorts into episodes. Optional.

evidence.quote: **Your org context and product facts**, including your claim rules
evidence.rationale: The optional org context supplies the claim rules that the Reddit answer planner in step 4 must follow.

evidence.quote: **Five to ten rivals** (optional)
evidence.rationale: An optional list of rivals is the competitor set. Step 1 receives it, and the panel records each brand as named, linked or absent.

evidence.quote: **Search data or past sales** (optional)
evidence.rationale: An optional search or sales export is the performance sheet. It helps the category plan pick and order the category.

evidence.quote: org context and product facts**, including your claim rules (optional)
evidence.rationale: Optional product facts give the true product details that answers and placements may state, kept inside the claim rules.

evidence.quote: **Your category**, with the collection page and three or four product pages (required)

evidence.rationale: The brief gives the goal, the reader, the angle, any required claims and the ad format with its character limit. Step 1 ad-headline-writer writes and checks the headline set against these.

evidence.quote: **Your live offer** (required): the price, the terms and the dates it runs.
evidence.rationale: The live offer's price, terms and dates go to all three steps. Step 2 writes stronger versions only from the offer's facts, and step 3 keys the test on it.

evidence.quote: **Your product's facts** (required): price, variants, what it is made of, how it is used, and what you can prove.
evidence.rationale: Product facts (price, variants, materials, use and proof) are what step 1 builds headlines from. No headline may add a claim the facts do not support.

evidence.quote: **A live offer with price and terms**: what the buyer pays and gets, and the dates it applies (required)
evidence.rationale: The live offer feeds step 1 and the keyed test plan, and limits headlines to claims the offer states.

evidence.quote: **Who your buyer is** (optional)
evidence.rationale: The buyer profile is given to step 1 to score buying reasons for fit with the real buyer.

evidence.quote: **One product's facts, with amounts, times, counts and dates** (required)
evidence.rationale: Product facts give each headline the real detail it must carry and feed steps 1 and 2.

evidence.quote: **Customer words** from reviews, tickets or surveys, with source and date (optional).

evidence.quote: **A buyer persona or your org context** (optional)

evidence.quote: **For each group, its size, what it costs to reach and who has bought what and when**

evidence.quote: **A buyer persona or your org context** (optional)

evidence.quote: **One product's facts**: price, what it does, how it is used, and what each order costs to make and deliver (required)
evidence.rationale: The product facts and cost per order feed all three steps. The test planner's break-even sums use the order cost.

evidence.quote: **Your question**: what you sell and the groups you could sell to (required)
evidence.rationale: The person's question names what they sell and the candidate groups. Step 1 ranks those groups from coldest to hungriest.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional): for rules on claims, price and fit
evidence.rationale: The org context's claim, price and fit rules feed the viability and value ratings without new facts being invented.

evidence.quote: **The idea, the problem it solves and who it is for** (required)
evidence.rationale: The product idea is what product-idea-risk-checker rates on the four risks in step 1.

evidence.quote: reviews, support messages, survey answers or call notes, pasted raw
evidence.rationale: Raw customer words with source and date are passed to step 1 as evidence for the value risk. Without them the rating stays unknown.

evidence.quote: **Rivals you already track** (optional)
evidence.rationale: Known competitors are passed to the rival mapper alongside the non-category rivals it finds for the job.

evidence.quote: **Product facts, reviews or support emails** (optional).
evidence.rationale: Product facts tell the job hunt what is sold, and feed the white-space ratings from the facts given.

evidence.quote: **Your question**, such as where growth could come from (required)
evidence.rationale: The user's question, such as where growth could come from, is given to the job-hunting step to aim the search.

evidence.quote: your question and any reviews or support emails
evidence.rationale: Customer reviews and support emails are given to step 1 to find workarounds and struggles that point to unmet jobs.

evidence.quote: your buyers and their words (review quotes and the doubts they raise), products and prices
evidence.rationale: The org context gives buyer words, products, offers and allowed claims; step 2 cannot map gaps without the buyer words, and the run stops without them.

evidence.quote: one row per ad, with spend, impressions, clicks, purchases, revenue, days live and the opening line

evidence.quote: **Your monthly Google budget, average order value and margin** (required for step 4).

evidence.rationale: The person's store details, checkout data and current tracking set up the tracking builder in step 1, the only thing needed to start.

evidence.quote: **Your Merchant Center products and issues export, with the product count** (required for step 3).
evidence.rationale: The Merchant Center products and issues export is the spreadsheet the feed health checker ranks by sales lost.

evidence.quote: **Test-order screenshots** (required for step 2): the Google Ads conversion page and Tag Assistant, from a real test order.
evidence.rationale: Screenshots from a real test order capture the store's tracking state, which the purchase tracking checker compares with the setup plan.

evidence.quote: If you attached an org context, read its `voice-and-look.md` for colors and fonts.

evidence.quote: **Event facts** (yours): name, date, time, place, price and how to book or attend.
evidence.rationale: The brief carries the event facts and where the poster will be seen, which set the reading order and every word printed.

evidence.quote: Use the brand colors and fonts if supplied.
evidence.rationale: Design tokens supply the exact colours and type the poster designer uses and the contrast checker tests.

evidence.quote: **Headline, primary text, description and CTA within platform limits** (optional)
evidence.rationale: Ad copy fields are sample copy that the brand voice editor in step 3 checks against the voice and rewrites.

evidence.quote: **A draft of any copy (ad, page, email or script) that a check or edit pass works on** (optional)
evidence.rationale: A copy draft is the sample text the step 3 voice editor checks line by line and rewrites with the org context's facts.

evidence.quote: **Ad or store performance export for a closed date window, with definitions** (optional)
evidence.rationale: An ad or store performance export is asked for as optional context; no step names it, so it only adds background to the audit.

evidence.quote: **One product's facts: price, variants, ingredients or materials, how it is used, photos by job** (optional)
evidence.rationale: One product's facts are optional context that can back the claims the org context builder records; no step requires them.

evidence.quote: Uses the org context from step 1 and your own ad copy or script, not step 2's report.
evidence.rationale: A video ad script is one form of sample copy the step 3 voice editor checks and rewrites.

evidence.quote: **Saved evidence from a storefront visit** (required): screenshots of your homepage, a product page, your packaging and one email
evidence.rationale: The dated storefront capture is what step 2 scores against the org context, touchpoint by touchpoint, so it is required.

evidence.quote: Reads your store and reviews into one org context.
evidence.rationale: Customer reviews are read with the store in step 1 to build the org context of voice, promise, buyers and claims.

evidence.quote: **A built or live web page, as a URL or saved HTML** (required).
evidence.rationale: The live store page is what step 1 reads into the org context and where each voice rule and claim cites its source page.

evidence.quote: If you have an org context, step 1 reads `offers.md` and `proof-and-claims.md` for facts
evidence.rationale: The org context's offers and claims files supply the facts behind each rewrite and the dates and limits for the ask.

evidence.quote: **A draft of any copy (ad, page, email or script) that a check or edit pass works on** (required)
evidence.rationale: The vague ad or page draft is the text step 1 rewrites line by line and later steps extend and edit.

evidence.quote: **A live offer with price, terms, effective_from/to and a current flag** (optional)
evidence.rationale: The live offer's real dates and limits give step 3 an honest reason to act now in the ask.

evidence.quote: **One product's facts: price, variants, ingredients or materials, how it is used, photos by job** (required)
evidence.rationale: The product facts from the products part are the details vague words get replaced with and the links in the how-it-works chain.

evidence.quote: **Your brand facts** (optional but strongly advised): name, buyers, offers and budget.
evidence.rationale: The brand facts the method asks for, name, buyers, offers and budget, are held in the org context files and feed the law check and bold move.

evidence.quote: **Your main rivals and what each is known for** (optional).
evidence.rationale: The rival list with what each is known for feeds the law check and lets the last step find where each rival is least ready.

evidence.quote: **Your marketing plan** (required), as written and as rough as it is.
evidence.rationale: The marketing plan is the main input every step reads, and each verdict quotes its lines.

evidence.quote: **Product facts for any new product in the plan** (needed if the plan adds one).

evidence.quote: An org context makes the result better but is not needed.
evidence.rationale: The org context can supply the brand facts and any name that must be kept, which step 3 uses when naming the category and brand.

evidence.quote: **Your main rivals and what each is known for.**
evidence.rationale: The rivals and what each holds build the white-space grid in step 1, which the category finder works from.

evidence.quote: **Your product facts:** price, benefits, proof and how it is used.
evidence.rationale: Product facts feed the white-space grid in step 1 and the press-first launch plan in step 4.

evidence.quote: **Customer words** from reviews, tickets or calls, with source and date.
evidence.rationale: Customer words from reviews or calls go to the white-space mapper and the launch planner to ground the open spots and the news angle.

evidence.quote: **Your org context**: facts, voice, offers and claims.
evidence.rationale: The org context gives facts, voice, current offers and claims to the problem list and the offer stack. If there is none, a MISSING: org context line is added.

evidence.quote: **Sales numbers or the buyer's own numbers,** such as their hourly rate or what a lost sale costs them.
evidence.rationale: Sales numbers and the buyer's own numbers let step 5 work out what the result is worth to the buyer and set a price band. Without them, the worth figure is marked as an estimate.

evidence.quote: **Who your buyer is and what they want,** or a buyer profile
evidence.rationale: The buyer profile gives the problem, triggers, wants and doubts. Step 1 turns these into every problem along the buyer's path, each with its driver and a promise.

evidence.quote: **Hours and cash you can spend delivering.**
evidence.rationale: A plan that states the hours and cash available for delivery sets the cost limit for trimming and stacking the offer in step 3. Without it, a one-hour-per-buyer default is used and marked MISSING.

evidence.quote: **Your product facts:** price, variants, how it is used.
evidence.rationale: Product facts give the price, variants and how the product is used. Step 1 uses them for the problem list, and steps 3 to 5 use them for the stack's margin and price ratio.

evidence.quote: **Reviews or call notes in the buyer's words,** with source and date.
evidence.rationale: Reviews and call notes give step 1 real problems in the buyer's own words, kept apart from guesses. Without them, the problems are marked as guesses.

evidence.quote: Headline, primary text, description and CTA within platform limits
evidence.rationale: Existing ad copy gives headline, primary text and CTA that the three offer ads and the Meta rules check can reuse. Optional.

evidence.quote: A landing page or advertorial: sections, copy, layout notes
evidence.rationale: A landing page shows where the offer ads send people, so the offer shown matches the page. Optional.

evidence.quote: Ad or store performance export for a closed date window, with definitions
evidence.rationale: A results export can show which offers and products already sell when picking the offer to build ads on. Optional.

evidence.quote: A buyer grounded in real review language: problem, trigger, wants, doubts, words they use
evidence.rationale: The buyers part of the org context gives the buyer's problem, doubts and words that shape how each ad shows the offer. Optional.

evidence.quote: One product's facts: price, variants, ingredients or materials, how it is used, photos by job
evidence.rationale: The products part of the org context gives the price and product facts the offer finder and ad planner work from. Optional.

evidence.quote: Photos of the real product, labelled by angle and use
evidence.rationale: Real product photos are needed so the three image ads show the true product; required.

evidence.quote: A video ad script, beat by beat, with on-screen text and shots
evidence.rationale: An existing video script can lend its approved on-screen lines and beats to the image ads' words. Optional.

evidence.quote: Customer words from reviews, tickets, surveys or calls, with source and date
evidence.rationale: Customer words with sources feed the org context build and give real buyer language for the offer ads. Optional.

evidence.quote: A built or live web page, as a URL or saved HTML
evidence.rationale: The website is what step 1 reads to build the org context with real prices, terms, colours and claims; required.

evidence.quote: **Your org context,** and visits split by source such as ads, email and search.
evidence.rationale: The optional org context is listed among the optional extras that support the page fixes. The run works without it.

evidence.quote: **Your page,** as a link, text or screenshots.
evidence.rationale: The required landing page, as a link, text or screenshots, is what step 1 reviews for the worst drop-off and what step 2 reads after the fix.

evidence.quote: **Visits and orders for the last few weeks,** as an export.
evidence.rationale: The required visits and orders export is the performance sheet. Step 3 sizes the A/B test from it after the second pause.

evidence.quote: **Customer words** (questions or reviews) copied as written, with source and date.
evidence.rationale: Required customer questions and reviews are passed to customer-question-finder in step 2 to build the OPEN DOUBTS list.

evidence.quote: **Your org context,** or a note on your offer, proof and buyer doubts.
evidence.rationale: An optional org context supplies the offer, proof and buyer doubts the step 2 auditor uses to judge whether the page answers them. It does not replace the page or the analytics.

evidence.quote: **Your landing page,** as a link, saved copy, or sections and copy.
evidence.rationale: The landing page is what step 2 landing-page-auditor reads like a stranger to produce ranked fixes. Step 1 can start without it, but the run stops at step 2 if it is missing.

evidence.quote: **Your analytics,** as an export for a closed date window with definitions
evidence.rationale: The analytics export (visits, steps and sales by page) lets step 1 plan the tracking check and drop-off review. Without it, the run stops at step 1.

evidence.quote: **Customer words** from reviews, tickets, surveys or calls, with source and date.
evidence.rationale: Optional customer words feed the research in step 1, including the questions to ask customers. They also serve as proof for issues, so each sorted problem has evidence, not only an opinion.

evidence.quote: **A built or live web page** as a URL or saved HTML.
evidence.rationale: An optional built or live web page lets the walk-through and audit check the real rendered page, not only its copy. Analytics and the page copy are still required.

evidence.quote: **Your brand facts:** voice, offers with effective dates, claims you may make, and look.
evidence.rationale: The org context supplies the voice, dated offers, allowed claims and look used across the script and brief.

evidence.quote: **Who the ad is for,** and the idea or angle you want to start from.
evidence.rationale: The brief names the buyer and the starting angle that step 1 turns into the ad's one argument.

evidence.quote: **The raw clips the creator filmed,** not edited ones, with their file names.
evidence.rationale: The creator's raw clips are what step 6 cuts into the timed edit plan after the pause.

evidence.quote: **a live offer** with price, terms and dates.
evidence.rationale: A live offer with price and dates gives the script's selling beat a real offer to name.

evidence.quote: **A buyer profile**
evidence.rationale: A buyer profile sharpens who the ad is for and their main doubt when step 1 picks the angle.

evidence.quote: **Your product facts:** price, variants, how it is used, and the claims you can back.
evidence.rationale: Product facts limit each spoken claim to what can be backed; without them the run stops at step 1.

evidence.quote: **Customer words** from reviews, tickets, surveys or calls, with source and date.
evidence.rationale: Customer words give the script the phrases buyers actually use, each with a source and date.

evidence.quote: step 3 uses it as the first screen of the signup page, with its headline, text and button within the platform's limits

evidence.quote: your facts, voice, products, offers with their dates, and the claims you may make
evidence.rationale: The org context goes to lead-magnet-planner in step 1 and to the page writer in step 3, for voice, offers and allowed claims.

evidence.quote: a short buyer brief with their problem, their stage, their doubts and the words they use

evidence.quote: Use real review or survey language, not guesses.

evidence.quote: so the email sounds like you and only makes claims you can back.

evidence.quote: **Your product and who it is for, with price, benefits and proof** (required)
evidence.rationale: Product facts with price, benefits and proof feed the position in step 1 and the launch plan's news angle in step 3.

evidence.quote: **What you want out of this, and what a good outcome looks like** (required)

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional)
evidence.rationale: The org context is passed to the social post planner in step 1 for voice and topics when the owner has one.

evidence.quote: **Your past posts' numbers** (optional, for the platform comparison in step 3)
evidence.rationale: A data file of past posts' counts gives step 3 a baseline to compare the two weeks against.

evidence.quote: **Who you want to reach** (optional)
evidence.rationale: The buyers part of the org context says who the posts should reach, which step 1 uses to set topics and post types.

evidence.quote: **The platforms you post on, and your goal** (required)
evidence.rationale: The owner's platforms and goal are the problem and good outcome the two-week calendar and results read are built around.

evidence.quote: Existing templates, and the owner of each update.
evidence.rationale: Existing message templates are copy drafts the update writer can start from, with the owner of each update.

evidence.quote: **What is affected and who**, from monitoring or the team lead.
evidence.rationale: The incident record of what is affected, who, and the timeline builds the fact ledger of confirmed, investigated and unknown items.

evidence.quote: **Communication rules**: who signs off, channels, tone.
evidence.rationale: The user's request sets the job scope: the audiences, sign-off person, channels and tone that the notices and updates are written for.

evidence.quote: **Mailing rules** (required): who gets this issue, the sender name, and the send date.

evidence.quote: **Customer messages** (required): reviews, emails, support chats or survey answers

evidence.quote: This method produces plan, brand guide, image prompt from the supplied brief.

evidence.quote: price, variants, ingredients or materials, how it is used and photos by job

evidence.quote: **Your product facts**: what it is, price, who uses it and what it solves.
evidence.rationale: The products part gives what it is, price and what it solves, which step 1 turns into the angle library.

evidence.quote: **Your customer words**: reviews, survey answers or support emails, with source and date.
evidence.rationale: Sourced reviews and survey answers are the customer words step 1 builds buyer problems and angles from; without them the run stops.

evidence.quote: **Notes from a newcomer's trial shift** (after the pause): every place they stopped, asked or guessed.
evidence.rationale: The newcomer's trial shift notes are feedback that step 3 turns into gaps with fixes before the ready call.

evidence.quote: **What you sell and how a customer gets it, from order to hand-off** (required): walk the path in a few lines.
evidence.rationale: The user's description of the shop and its customer path is the question the standards step starts from.

evidence.quote: The spreadsheet is the optional takings and costs sheet.
evidence.rationale: The takings and costs sheet for a week away lets step 3 say whether the shop earns without the owner.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (required): your facts, voice and colours.
evidence.rationale: The store's org context gives the facts, voice and colours used for the slot copy and the design plan.

evidence.quote: the person's org context, offer and product facts
evidence.rationale: The offer is given to the layout step so the slot map can carry the person's own offer instead of the admired page's.

evidence.quote: **Your product facts** (optional): price, variants and what it is made of.
evidence.rationale: Product facts give the price and variants the Shopify build step loads into the page.

evidence.quote: **A full-page screenshot of the page you admire** (required): the whole page, not a cropped one.
evidence.rationale: The reference set is the screenshot of the admired page whose section order and jobs are borrowed for the layout.

evidence.quote: "Store capture" means screenshots of your own store
evidence.rationale: The store capture is screenshots of the person's own store and live page, which the audit step reads for findings.

evidence.quote: "Your data" is the post export for step 4.
evidence.rationale: The dataset is the export of at least 20 posts with format, hook, date and views that the organic format tester reads in step 4.

evidence.quote: "Your question" in the list above means your accounts, product and buyer.
evidence.rationale: The question port carries the accounts, product and buyer answers that steps 1 to 3 check, pick formats for and score hooks against.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional): voice, banned claims and look.
evidence.rationale: The org context supplies the voice, banned claims and look. It is passed to the buyer brief writer in step 1 and limits every ad's wording.

evidence.quote: **Your product facts** (required): one product with its price, variants, ingredients or materials
evidence.rationale: Product facts with their price and allowed claims feed the selling points list in buying order. They are then passed to the story, carousel and image ad steps as the facts each one may use.

evidence.quote: **Customer reviews** (required): copied as written, with source and date.
evidence.rationale: Customer reviews give the buyer's moment and the four forces in the brief. Their quotes go word for word into the story image ad. With no reviews, the run stops.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (required): voice, look, products, offers and approved claims.
evidence.rationale: The required org context supplies voice, look and approved claims to the angle, script and clip-prompt steps. The character sheet is checked against it.

evidence.quote: **Your product facts** (required): price, variants, ingredients or materials, how it is used
evidence.rationale: Product facts and claim IDs are the only claims the script and the ad rules check may test against.

evidence.quote: **Who the ad is for** (required): the buyer and what a good ad does, in a line or two.
evidence.rationale: The person's question is who the ad is for and what a good ad does. Step 1 turns it into the angle brief.

evidence.quote: **Customer reviews** (optional): they make the buyer's doubt and the lines truer.
evidence.rationale: Optional customer reviews are given to the script step so the buyer's doubt and the spoken lines use real customer language.

evidence.quote: **A cost or process report, or a sheet of your costs and volumes** (optional).
evidence.rationale: An optional cost or process report adds cost lines and volumes for step 1 to mark as needed or not. It can also add process findings for the step 2 layout.

evidence.quote: **Rivals and their prices** (optional): include the far-off store people use today.
evidence.rationale: An optional rival set with prices lets step 1 show where rivals are thin and test whether the target price is reachable.

evidence.quote: the document is how the work runs now
evidence.rationale: The required document describes how the work runs now: steps in order, who does each, space, tools and stopwatch times. Step 2 work-flow-layout-planner rebuilds the layout from it.

evidence.quote: **The price you want to sell at** (required): a number or a group of customers and what they can pay now.
evidence.rationale: The question port carries the target price or buyer group and what is fixed. Step 1 works backward from it. With no target, step 1 writes MISSING: target price or buyer and asks.

evidence.quote: the spreadsheet is your product facts and cost lines (a pasted list works too)
evidence.rationale: The required spreadsheet holds product facts and cost lines per unit. Step 1 marks each line as needed, partly needed or not needed, with a saving. Thin cost lines make the plan provisional.

evidence.quote: **your ad or store results** (optional)
evidence.rationale: Ad or store results are given to step 1 so the org context's facts and claims are truer.

evidence.quote: **Who the photos are for** (optional)
evidence.rationale: The buyer profile tells step 3 who the flash snapshots are for and makes the org context truer.

evidence.quote: **Product facts and your colour codes** (optional).
evidence.rationale: Product facts and colour codes feed the org context so prompts use real details and brand colours.

evidence.quote: **Photos of your real product** (required): from the front, the back and in use
evidence.rationale: The real product photos keep shape, colour and printing true in every prompt across all three looks.

evidence.quote: **A photo whose look you like** (optional): the reference for step 4.
evidence.rationale: The admired photo is the reference whose light and mood step 4 copies onto the owner's product.

evidence.quote: **customer reviews** (optional)
evidence.rationale: Customer reviews go into the step 1 org context build so claims and buyer details are grounded.

evidence.quote: **Your website** (required): a link to your site, or the saved pages.
evidence.rationale: The website is what step 1 builds the org context from, giving prices, colours and product details.

evidence.quote: **One screen or prototype** (required): a screenshot, a Figma link or a clear description.
evidence.rationale: The design file or screenshot of one screen is what the usability reviewer checks in step 1. Every issue must point to a place on it.

evidence.quote: and the task they are trying to do (required). This is "your question" above.
evidence.rationale: The question names who uses the screen and the task they are trying to do. The review is run against that task, and the test tasks in step 3 check it.

evidence.quote: If your AI cannot open a link, ask for a screenshot.
evidence.rationale: A link to a live web page can be the screen under review. If the AI cannot open the link, it asks for a screenshot of that page instead.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional): voice, claims and offers you already have.
evidence.rationale: The org context supplies the voice, claims and existing offers used in the checker wording and the pitch.

evidence.quote: **Your main offer and its price** (required)
evidence.rationale: The live offer and price are what step 3's paid first step and pitch lead to.

evidence.quote: **After the pause, for step 2** (required): your ad or post spend, sign-ups
evidence.rationale: The campaign results for one to two weeks give the spend and sign-ups step 2 turns into cost per qualified lead.

evidence.quote: **Your service and your buyer** (required): what you sell, who has the problem it fixes
evidence.rationale: The user's question is the service, buyer and problem the free checker in step 1 is built around.

evidence.quote: Also uses your org context and offer, and hands the page to step 4.
evidence.rationale: The org context gives the voice and facts step 3 writes the landing page from; without it the run asks for the facts and marks gaps.

evidence.quote: that go with the ad (required). Paste them in full.
evidence.rationale: The ad's headline and primary text are the draft step 1 critiques and fixes, and that steps 2 to 4 rewrite and check.

evidence.quote: It takes the ad image and its headline and primary text.
evidence.rationale: The attached image ad is what the static ad critic scores for eye path and page match; the run stops without it.

evidence.quote: what you sell, the real price, shipping, returns and any guarantee.
evidence.rationale: The offer's real price and terms are what the page's cost block states in full; the run stops with no offer facts.

evidence.quote: The questions you answer every week** (required), and your real reply to each one.
evidence.rationale: The method says the question input means the weekly customer questions, each with the owner's real reply; one help page is written per question.

evidence.quote: Your current docs, FAQ, tickets or chats** (optional): the sources step 1 checks.
evidence.rationale: The method says source text means the store's own docs and tickets; step 1 gathers sourced answers from them and step 5 checks pages against them.

evidence.quote: **Raw or generated video clips to edit** (required for step 5 only)
evidence.rationale: Footage is the finished clip files the edit planner cuts by real file in step 5, after the filming pause.

evidence.quote: **A live offer with its price, terms, and start and end dates** (optional)
evidence.rationale: A live offer with terms and dates can be used in the script's offer part; without it no offer is invented.

evidence.quote: **One product's facts: price, variants, ingredients or materials, how it is used, photos by job** (required)
evidence.rationale: Product facts are what the VSL ad scripter turns, with the review words, into the seven-part script in step 1.

evidence.quote: **Customer words from reviews, tickets, surveys or calls, with source and date** (required)
evidence.rationale: Reviews and tickets with sources give the real customer words quoted in the script; no review may be invented.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional, recommended). Your products, voice and the claims you may make.
evidence.rationale: The org context's products, voice, offers and claims let steps 2 to 4 mark gaps that fit and write briefs with claims the brand may make.

evidence.quote: **Your own ad results** (optional). An export for a closed date window
evidence.rationale: An ad account export for set dates keeps the briefs in step 3 from repeating what already failed.

evidence.quote: **A rival's ads from the Meta Ad Library** (required).
evidence.rationale: The rival's ads are the reference ads counted in step 1 and read for gaps in step 2.

evidence.quote: An export or a hand-collected list with ad copy, format, start date and destination link, inactive ads included.
evidence.rationale: When the rival ads arrive as an exported or hand-built sheet with copy, format, start date and link columns, that sheet is what step 1 counts.

evidence.quote: **The rough notes** (required): pasted text or files.
evidence.rationale: The rough notes are the source document every claim in the handout must trace to, and they stay untouched.

evidence.quote: **The reader and the action** (required): who gets the handout and what they should understand or do after.
evidence.rationale: The method says the question is the reader, the action and the format, which step 1 organises the notes around.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional): it adds voice and approved claims.
evidence.rationale: The org context adds voice and approved claims to the scripts and compliance check; the run works without it.

evidence.quote: **Your posts with views and dates** (required): from your own account or from creators. This is the performance export.
evidence.rationale: The posts-with-views export is the performance sheet step 1 ranks against the median to pick outliers worth promoting.

evidence.quote: "your question" is your product facts and offer
evidence.rationale: The method maps the question input to the product facts and current offer, which the scripts, briefs and test plan rely on.

evidence.quote: **Two or three lessons you trust, each in one sentence** (required).
evidence.rationale: The body maps the question to the person's lessons, audience and time; the lessons are what each story and the talk are built on.

evidence.quote: **Your org context, and what you love to do** (optional, but step 2 needs it).
evidence.rationale: The org context supplies what the business offers, for whom and what it can prove, which answers the six prompts in the only-ness step.

evidence.quote: **Your rivals** (required). Include anything buyers might use instead of you
evidence.rationale: The rival list, including substitutes, is the competitor set mapped against buyer-valued features to find the white space.

evidence.quote: **The people who can say yes or no to the idea, and what you want them to do next** (required).
evidence.rationale: The user's ask, who must say yes and what they should do, frames the buy-in plan built in step 3.

evidence.quote: Reviews, notes or quotes from buyers in your category.
evidence.rationale: Buyer reviews and quotes show what buyers value in their own words and set the features in the white-space grid.

evidence.quote: It takes why visitors left, your conversion rate and your proof and offer.
evidence.rationale: The offer and guarantee are given to step 1 so each objection ad uses only an offer the store really has.

evidence.quote: **Your spend and new-customer revenue by channel** (required), for a closed date window
evidence.rationale: Channel spend and new-customer revenue are the performance sheet step 3 uses to cap retargeting spend.

evidence.quote: **Your product list with margins** (required). A sheet from your store or costing file: product, price and cost or margin.
evidence.rationale: The spreadsheet of products and margins lets step 2 pair cross-sell products by margin.

evidence.quote: **Why visitors left** (required). Reviews, survey answers, support questions or call notes, in the buyer's own words
evidence.rationale: Reviews and survey answers give the reasons visitors left, which step 1 splits into objections for each ad.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (required). Your claims and proof with sources, your guarantee and offer, and any banned claims.
evidence.rationale: The org context supplies sourced claims, proof, offer and banned claims that the long-form script writer uses in step 1.

evidence.quote: **Your brief** (required). Why people buy, the length you want (60 seconds to 10 minutes)
evidence.rationale: The brief sets why people buy, length, placement and buyer awareness for the narrated script in step 1.

evidence.quote: **A buyer description and customer words** (optional, helps).
evidence.rationale: A buyer persona gives the problem in the buyer's words, their doubts and the moment it hurts, which sharpen the script's problems and doubts.

evidence.quote: **Your product facts** (required). How it works, how it is used, price and variants
evidence.rationale: Product facts feed the script in step 1 and the shot list in step 4, including the real thing to show on screen.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (required). Your voice, products, offers and what you can claim.
evidence.rationale: The org context is read before the first draft. It gives the story email writer the brand's voice, products, offers and allowed claims.

evidence.quote: **A short brief with the goal of the email** (optional).
evidence.rationale: A brief gives the email's goal. That shapes the one action and the call to action in the three story drafts.

evidence.quote: **Your campaign numbers, exported after the send** (required for step 4 only).
evidence.rationale: The exported campaign numbers for the story email and the usual sends are read in step 4. They show whether the story email beat the usual sends, with a ranked diagnosis.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional). Your facts, claims and voice.
evidence.rationale: The org context gives the brand's facts, claims and voice that the alternative page may use. Optional.

evidence.quote: **The names of one to five rivals** (required).
evidence.rationale: The competitor set is the one to five rivals whose public pages step 1 reads and compares.

evidence.quote: **Your product facts and where you honestly win** (optional).
evidence.rationale: The products part of the org context gives price, features and proof; the page uses only facts given. Optional.

evidence.quote: Say the one buyer question you want the page to answer, if you have one.
evidence.rationale: The question is the one buyer question the alternative page should answer. Optional.

evidence.quote: Reviews, tickets, survey answers or call notes, with source and date.
evidence.rationale: Customer words about the choice feed the white space map in step 2 and show where you honestly win. Optional.

evidence.quote: **Your org context or buyer profile** (optional)
evidence.rationale: The optional org context supplies facts, voice and claims that step 1 may use when it builds the why-first message.

evidence.quote: **Each no you heard** (needed for step 4, after the pause). Who said it, when, and their words.
evidence.rationale: Feedback notes are the recorded nos from the pause: who said it and their words. Step 4 sorts them into the doubt log.

evidence.quote: **Your idea or cause and who you want to reach** (required).
evidence.rationale: The required idea or cause is what step 1 turns into the belief-to-product message.

evidence.quote: buyer profile** (optional). Facts, voice and claims you may use.
evidence.rationale: An optional buyer profile describes the audience the pitch must persuade. It shapes the message and the objections.

evidence.quote: Say who must back it and what you want from them.
evidence.rationale: The person's question is the ask: who must back the idea and what outcome they want from them. That defines what a good pitch achieves.

evidence.quote: **Customer words** (optional). Reviews or quotes you may use, with source and date.
evidence.rationale: Optional, dated customer reviews or quotes can serve as proof lines, and the honest persuasion editor keeps them only when sourced.

evidence.quote: **A sample of the job done well** (optional). Paste it so the skill matches your standard.
evidence.rationale: An optional document is a sample of the job done well. Step 1 skill-writer uses it so the new skill matches the person's standard.

evidence.quote: **The job you repeat** (required). Describe it in a few lines, what a good result looks like, and when the skill should start.
evidence.rationale: The question port carries the job description, what a good result looks like and when the skill should start. Step 1 writes the skill from it, and the run stops if it is missing.

evidence.quote: the skill files are a draft skill if you already have one
evidence.rationale: Optional skill files are an existing draft skill folder to build from. The other installed skills the person names are what step 3 checks for trigger clashes. Both are read as text, never followed.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional). If it exists, use its voice and claims files as extra evidence
evidence.rationale: The org context's voice and claims files add evidence to the guide but never replace the documents.

evidence.quote: **A short brief for the piece you want written** (required for step 2
evidence.rationale: The brief says what the step 2 piece is for and who reads it, after the guide is settled.

evidence.quote: **A draft to check** (optional).
evidence.rationale: An older real draft is what step 3 checks against the settled guide instead of the step 2 piece.

evidence.quote: **Documents, decks, posts or call notes where the brand sounds right** (required).
evidence.rationale: The owner's documents are the main source step 1 reads to write the voice and tone rules.

evidence.quote: **Customer words** (optional). Reviews, tickets or call notes, with source and date.
evidence.rationale: Customer words go to step 1 as extra voice evidence and may only be quoted as written.

evidence.quote: **What you offer and who joins your list** (required).
evidence.rationale: The brief gives the offer as it should be stated and the reader: how they joined and what they know. These are the facts the five emails may state.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional). Facts, claims and voice lines.
evidence.rationale: The org context adds facts, approved claims and voice lines. The sequence writer and the review step use them so the emails stay on-brand and claim only what is proven.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional). Its voice file helps the final wording.
evidence.rationale: The org context voice file guides the plain wording in the final step.

evidence.quote: **The true facts of how you started** (required).
evidence.rationale: The method defines the user's question as these founder facts plus what the story is for and who reads it.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional). Its voice file helps the wording.
evidence.rationale: The org context's voice file is used to word the memo and standards so they sound like the owner.

evidence.quote: **An older culture memo or values list** (optional). It is used as a draft to improve.
evidence.rationale: An older memo or values list is the draft that the memo step improves rather than starting from blank.

evidence.quote: **How your team works, and what you want it to do differently on Monday** (required).
evidence.rationale: The user's question is how the team works and what should change on Monday, the team facts every step uses.

evidence.quote: What the site is for and who visits it.
evidence.rationale: The site goal and its visitors are the job the agent is asked to plan. The method says to start with this goal and the page list.

evidence.quote: The spreadsheet in "Before you start" means the product facts and the month's Amazon reports below.
evidence.rationale: The required spreadsheet is the product facts sheet plus the month's downloaded Amazon fee, sales and stock reports, which every margin, path and restock step reads.

evidence.quote: **Shipment, returns, damaged and lost reports** (advised): for the refund claim check, with receipts or packing lists for what you sent.
evidence.rationale: These dated Seller Central report exports are the optional results data the claim finder step reads; without them the method says the claim check was not run.

evidence.quote: Run `amazon-keyword-picker` on the new keyword export, then `amazon-listing-writer`.
evidence.rationale: A keyword export with search terms and volumes is the keyword list the listing refresh path feeds to the keyword picker; without it the refresh waits.

evidence.quote: The full case and its exhibits.
evidence.rationale: The case pack and its exhibits are the source document every evidence check is held against. The agent reads it in full before it reviews the deck.

evidence.quote: The team's recommendation and current deck (or its text).
evidence.rationale: The team's current deck is what the agent reviews against the rubric and the exhibits, and it revises the slides a change touches.

evidence.quote: **Last month's numbers** (required): campaign list with send date, recipients, opens, clicks, orders and revenue.
evidence.rationale: The monthly campaign and flow export is the dated results sheet the keeper compares month on month before it decides what to fix.

evidence.quote: **Your live flows** (required the first time): each flow's trigger, filters, delay and number of emails.
evidence.rationale: The live flows with their trigger, timing and emails are the flows the keeper checks and saves as its flows file after the first run.

evidence.quote: **Org context, offer and product facts** (optional, needed for a rebuild)
evidence.rationale: The org context gives the voice and claims a flow rebuild must follow. The method says it is needed only when a flow is rebuilt.

evidence.quote: voice, claims, discount room, best sellers.
evidence.rationale: The live offer sets the discount room a rebuilt flow may use. The method asks for it with the org context when a flow is rebuilt.

evidence.quote: **Org context, offer and product facts** (optional, needed for a rebuild): voice, claims, discount room, best sellers.
evidence.rationale: Product facts name the best sellers a rebuilt flow can feature. The method asks for them only when a flow needs a rebuild.

evidence.quote: **Last month's tickets** (required): the export, with the customer's question, the reply that solved it, the date
evidence.rationale: The ticket export is customer words with dates, which is what the keeper reads to find the questions the help centre fails to answer.

evidence.quote: **The help centre** (required): every article as text, with its address and last-updated date.
evidence.rationale: The help centre articles are the documents the keeper checks for gaps, age and clarity, and the ones it proposes to change.

evidence.quote: **Org context** (advised): voice and facts, for the voice check.
evidence.rationale: The org context gives the voice and facts the articles are checked against. Without it the method checks the articles for clarity only.

evidence.quote: **Search Console export** (required): queries and pages for last month with clicks, impressions, average position and click rate.
evidence.rationale: The Search Console export is the query report every check reads, from quick wins to the post outlines, each tied to a query in it.

evidence.quote: **Your site address and page list** (required): so the basics check and the thin-page check know what exists.
evidence.rationale: The site address and page list tell the keeper which pages exist, so the basics and thin-page checks look at real pages.

evidence.quote: **A read-only connection to your site** (optional): so thin pages can be read directly.
evidence.rationale: A read-only site connection lets the keeper open thin pages itself instead of asking the owner to paste them.

evidence.quote: **Org context** (optional): facts and voice, for any rewrite.
evidence.rationale: The org context gives the facts and voice a page rewrite must keep. The method uses it only when it rewrites a page.

evidence.quote: **The items to look at** (required): the posts you might reply to, or the comments on your own posts
evidence.rationale: The posts and comments to answer are the short texts the desk sorts and writes replies to, with who wrote each and when.

evidence.quote: **What you stand for and what you will not say** (optional): your org context, or a few lines on topics to avoid.
evidence.rationale: The org context tells the desk what the owner stands for and which topics to avoid, so no reply says something off brand.

evidence.quote: **Search term insights** (required).
evidence.rationale: The Performance Max exports, starting with search term insights and product spend, are the results data every weekly check reads.

evidence.quote: **The launch plan** (optional): from the Performance Max launch planner, so the live campaign is checked against what was planned.
evidence.rationale: The launch plan lets the keeper compare the live campaign with what was planned and flag where it has drifted.

evidence.quote: The optional spreadsheet named above is where you may keep the four money numbers below
evidence.rationale: The spreadsheet holds the break-even CPA, break-even ROAS, blended MER and new-customer CPA that the checks judge results against.

evidence.quote: **Quiz submissions export** (required): one row per person, one column per question.
evidence.rationale: The quiz export is the spreadsheet of answers the skill reads to find what buyers want and turn it into ad angles.

evidence.quote: **Ad sets that sent the traffic** (optional).
evidence.rationale: The ad sets that sent the traffic let the skill tie answer patterns to where the people came from. It is optional context from the ad account.

evidence.quote: **Approved words** (optional): the exact words, where they sit, and which is biggest.
evidence.rationale: Approved ad words are placed in the image exactly as given, with their position and size, so the prompt never makes up text.

evidence.quote: Before writing MISSING for a fact, look for it in the org context and the input
evidence.rationale: The org context is where the skill looks for product facts, colours and claims before it marks any gap as missing.

evidence.quote: **The approved ad** (required): the chosen scene, layout and image shape.
evidence.rationale: The approved ad concept is the brief the image prompt is built from: the scene, the layout and the image shape.

evidence.quote: **The mistakes list** (optional): rules from earlier jobs.
evidence.rationale: The mistakes list carries lessons from earlier image jobs, which the skill applies so the same errors are not repeated.

evidence.quote: **Product photos** (required whenever the product is in shot)
evidence.rationale: Real product photos, one per role, keep the product in the image true to the item sold. The method asks for photos, not a description.

evidence.quote: **A customer list** (required): one row per customer, with these columns: customer name or ID, total amount paid, and months as a customer
evidence.rationale: The customer list is what the skill sorts by amount paid and time as a customer to find the top fifth.

evidence.quote: **Survey answers or reviews** (optional): goals, why they bought, where they heard of you.
evidence.rationale: Survey answers and reviews give the top group's own words on goals and reasons to buy, which step 3 reads and quotes.

evidence.quote: **Your org context** (optional).
evidence.rationale: The method asks for the org context, and the shared org context read list says which parts to use, such as voice, claims and buyers. Here it adds the brand's known buyers and offers to compare with the profile.

evidence.quote: **Buyer evidence** (required): reviews, support messages, survey answers, call notes, cancellation reasons, forum posts.
evidence.rationale: Reviews, support messages and call notes are the customer words the brief is built from, quote by quote.

evidence.quote: **The org context** (optional): voice, offers, approved claims, buyer groups, what competitors promise.
evidence.rationale: The org context gives the voice, approved claims, buyer groups and rival promises the brief must agree with.

evidence.quote: the notes are the question.
evidence.rationale: The method says the meeting notes are the question here. The card is built from what the person said and what was promised.

evidence.quote: **A brief on the person** (optional).
evidence.rationale: A short brief on the one person met adds what they care about to the card. It is a profile of one person, not a buyer group.

evidence.quote: **A brief on the person** (required): what they care about, what to admire, the question only they can answer.
evidence.rationale: The brief on the person is a profile of one individual: what they care about and what to ask them. The whole plan is built on it.

evidence.quote: **Your aim** (optional).
evidence.rationale: The aim is what the user wants from the talk, which the plan steers the questions toward when it is given.

evidence.quote: **The original ad** (required): a screenshot of each shot or part (or the image itself), with its time, spoken words and on-screen lines
evidence.rationale: The original ad, shot by shot with its spoken words and on-screen lines, is the script the planner remakes as a still or carousel.

evidence.quote: **Brief** (required): still or carousel, the size (4:5 or 1:1), the number of cards if fixed, where it runs.
evidence.rationale: The brief sets the format, size, card count and placement, which is the formats part of a creative brief. The words stay locked.

evidence.quote: **Org context** (works best; without it, ask once for the product facts and carry on with `MISSING:` marks)
evidence.rationale: The org context gives the product facts, claims, live offer, fonts and colours the remake must keep.

evidence.quote: **Product photos** (optional, needed if the product appears): front, side, top, out of the pack, in a hand.
evidence.rationale: Product photos keep the product true in the remade picture. The method reads them directly, like the frames.

evidence.quote: **Brand facts** (required): voice, claims with sources, live offers only, guarantee, the never-show list, the brand's look.

catalogue-items/imported/incident-postmo.input_quote: Walk me through the process — describe it, paste existing docs, or just tell me the name
catalogue-items/imported/incident-postmo.rationale: The verified postmortem can be supplied as existing documentation for a remediation procedure. The user still needs to select the process and provide its owner and missing operating details.
catalogue-items/imported/incident-postmo.condition: Use reviewed incident facts and a user-selected remediation process. A postmortem alone is not a complete operating procedure.

catalogue-items/imported/expo-upgrade-he.input_quote: run from an Expo project directory (the command resolves the project ID from `app.json`).
catalogue-items/imported/expo-upgrade-he.rationale: The same Expo project can supply project identity after the approved upgrade changes are applied. Monitoring is a later published-update follow-up; the upgrade does not itself publish or supply metrics.
catalogue-items/imported/expo-upgrade-he.adaptation: Reuse the original project with the reviewed upgrade changes applied. Read its app.json project identity. Do not treat a written migration plan as an updated codebase.
catalogue-items/imported/expo-upgrade-he.condition: Only after an approved EAS update is actually published and authorized EAS access plus a real update/channel identifier are available. Otherwise stop the monitoring step.

catalogue-items/general/availability-pay.output_quote: Run the bundled script or build a workbook only when you have code or file tools and the person wants one.
catalogue-items/general/availability-pay.rationale: A requested workbook can carry the verified payment and operating-cash calculation into the bridge. It supplies only part of the financial evidence, not the financing definition, taxes, working capital or a complete model.
catalogue-items/general/availability-pay.condition: The person requested a workbook, file tools were available, and the actual workbook was made and reviewed. Match period, units and cash-versus-invoice basis before reusing its figures.

catalogue-items/general/lead-offer-tuner.output_quote: Write the new title, the offer text, and where it sits in the ad.
catalogue-items/general/lead-offer-tuner.input_quote: The offer the ad named, under the same name and at the same price.
catalogue-items/general/lead-offer-tuner.rationale: The tuned reply offer's title, wording and terms pass to the page writer's offer port, so the landing page keeps the same offer the ad shows. The writer still needs the approved business facts, org context and the real ad. The tuner's predictions stay guesses, and any fee or no-call condition must stay as stated.

catalogue-items/general/motion-graphics-.output_quote: how the product looks, colours, fonts, photo style, and the exact words allowed on the picture
catalogue-items/general/motion-graphics-.input_quote: font files, logo as a vector file, colour codes
catalogue-items/general/motion-graphics-.rationale: An image-work slice of the org context passes the recorded colours, fonts and logo file names, plus the words allowed on screen, into the look card and lock lines. Stale or unconfirmed lines do not pass. The planner still needs the script and real product cutout files. A missing font or logo file stays a gap, and no credentials or spend approval are created.

catalogue-items/general/reason-why-deal-.output_quote: *Writing:* the chosen offer facts, approved claims with their conditions, buyer quotes, voice lines.
catalogue-items/general/reason-why-deal-.input_quote: **Your org context** (optional): voice and claims you can make.
catalogue-items/general/reason-why-deal-.rationale: A writing slice of the org context passes approved claims with their conditions, voice lines and buyer quotes. Stale, unconfirmed and banned lines stay out. The deal writer still needs the required buyer shortlist and the product facts: a real deal, costs and dates. The slice does not authorise a promotion or turn a pending claim into proof.

catalogue-items/general/static-html-land.adaptation: Open the actual current HTML preview, extract its complete visible page copy in reading order and attach current phone screenshots of the first screen and buy area as the landing_page input. Carry checks.md as observations, not a substitute for inspecting the preview.
catalogue-items/general/static-html-land.output_quote: index.html, styles.css and an assets/ folder, plus checks.md (what was checked and how) and README.md (how to preview, host and set up the form).
catalogue-items/general/static-html-land.input_quote: **The page** (required): its text top to bottom and, if you can, phone screenshots of the first screen and the buy area.
catalogue-items/general/static-html-land.rationale: The web_page source is adapted into the actual readable landing_page that the checker consumes. No ad, verified offer facts or speed report is synthesized, and unavailable checks remain explicit.
catalogue-items/general/static-html-land.condition: Proceed once the actual preview or complete page text is available; mark unseen imagery, behavior and speed checks can't tell and never infer a launch or completed submission from source alone.

catalogue-items/general/static-html-land.output_quote: Create index.html, styles.css and a local assets/ folder.
catalogue-items/general/static-html-land.input_quote: for raw HTML strings, files (`Read` first, then `audit_html`), or JSX you've rendered to a string.
catalogue-items/general/static-html-land.rationale: The built index.html and styles.css pass as the web page to audit, and checks.md shows what was already checked by hand. The checker must use tools that are really installed and must state that coverage is limited without a live DOM. It edits files only if the owner asked for fixes. No conformance claim follows.

catalogue-items/imported/animated-landin.adaptation: Extract the visible headline, subtext, feature bullets, button and closing copy from the produced HTML into a labelled existing-page draft, keep every CONFIRM CLAIM tag, and check each fact against the approved org context and real offer before reuse.
catalogue-items/imported/animated-landin.output_quote: Generate a polished, self-contained `.html` landing page from a text prompt or brief.
catalogue-items/imported/animated-landin.input_quote: Read the existing page before rewriting, retain correct brand language and working buyer choices
catalogue-items/imported/animated-landin.rationale: The generated HTML page passes as an existing draft whose copy the writer rewrites to match an ad. It does not supply the writer's required offer and facts or the org context, and its invented or CONFIRM CLAIM content is not evidence. The writer's output is copy, so the page must be rebuilt after.

catalogue-items/imported/page-transition.adaptation: Only when the owner separately asks for a new React landing page in the same app: add the transition patch, the touched component paths and the reduced-motion CSS to that request as existing-work context, so the new page reuses the wrapper. Keep the owner's page brief and product facts as their own input.
catalogue-items/imported/page-transition.output_quote: When adding view transitions to an existing app, **follow `references/implementation.md` step by step.**
