tools/orchestrator-pages/draft-your-due-.rationale: The final document passes on the draft ledger, each draft's task ID and thread ID, send status and missing facts. The register reads them as open follow-ups to track. It still needs the date window, timezone and today's date. Message IDs and sent status can only be added after the person sends. An approved draft is not proof of sending, and the handoff gives no permission to change tasks.

tools/orchestrator-pages/draft-your-due-.adaptation: Turn the draft ledger into one row per task ID with owner, due date, thread ID and state; count a follow-up as done only when the owner sent it and a message ID is recorded, and flag drafted or waiting items as open.
tools/orchestrator-pages/draft-your-due-.output_quote: **Draft ledger:** each draft's version, state and message ID, so a rerun does not send twice.
tools/orchestrator-pages/draft-your-due-.input_quote: Step 1 takes the week's meeting notes, email threads and task list, plus last week's action list.
tools/orchestrator-pages/draft-your-due-.rationale: The follow-up drafts and ledger pass each due task's ID, thread, recipient and send state as evidence of this week's follow-ups. The weekly review still needs the week's real meeting notes and threads, the week dates and next week's calendar. An unsent draft is not proof of sending.

tools/orchestrator-pages/leave-job-own-i.adaptation: Lift what the person sells, the fee and billing terms from step 2, and the client cap and hours from the plan into the offer builder's product and price facts. Delivery cost per client is marked MISSING unless the plan states it.
tools/orchestrator-pages/leave-job-own-i.output_quote: Choose a fee in the top third of the prices with a reason you can say aloud.
tools/orchestrator-pages/leave-job-own-i.input_quote: **Product and price facts** (required): what is sold, the price, what each unit or period costs you, delivery cost.
tools/orchestrator-pages/leave-job-own-i.rationale: The plan's service, fee and terms give the offer builder its product and price facts. It still needs one named buyer with their doubt in their own words (persona, required), for example from the first-client notes, and the exact guarantee and terms. The plan does not invent these.

catalogue-items/orchestrators/plan-an-ev.output_quote: Each row has an id, task, owner, due date, status and the source note.
catalogue-items/orchestrators/plan-an-ev.input_quote: each task with its due date, owner and status, as an export or paste.
catalogue-items/orchestrators/plan-an-ev.rationale: The promise register (action-register.csv) passes on as the due task list for the next round of follow-ups. The next workflow also needs the matching email thread and recipient for each task. Event promises often have none, and those tasks get MISSING: thread with no draft. The hold list and contact consent carry over, and no permission is created.

tools/orchestrator-pages/prepare-a-price.output_quote: Step 4 file: your opening lines, your questions, a safe-no question and what to listen for. This is the plan for the call.
tools/orchestrator-pages/prepare-a-price.input_quote: **A plan so far** (optional): the opening lines, limits and fallback already set
tools/orchestrator-pages/prepare-a-price.rationale: The call plan passes the opening lines, proposed sum and walk-away line as limits to stay inside; the next skill still needs the situation, including what you cannot accept and where you are weak.

catalogue-items/orchestrators/prepare-a-.adaptation: Take the CUSTOMER QUESTION block from the newsletter hand-back (the grouped question, the word-for-word quote with its source, the count and sample limits) together with the original dated customer messages it came from, and pass them as the customer reviews and questions for the topic bank. Mark the newsletter's own topic and send date so the calendar does not repeat it.
catalogue-items/orchestrators/prepare-a-.output_quote: Copy one quote exactly, with its source.
catalogue-items/orchestrators/prepare-a-.input_quote: **Customer reviews and questions** with source and date.
catalogue-items/orchestrators/prepare-a-.rationale: The newsletter hand-back passes the real customer question, its exact quote with source and the message count, which the topic bank can use as customer questions. The month planner still needs product facts, the org context and the brief written at its pause; nothing is approved or sent by the handoff.

catalogue-items/orchestrators/prepare-a-.adaptation: Turn the hand-back's customer question, quote with source and count into a short brief whose goal is a story email answering that question, with the list and one action named. Do not reuse the newsletter draft as the story email or invent a story to fit.
catalogue-items/orchestrators/prepare-a-.output_quote: Question | exact quote and source | <number> of <number> messages | sample limits
catalogue-items/orchestrators/prepare-a-.input_quote: A short brief with the goal of the email
catalogue-items/orchestrators/prepare-a-.rationale: The customer question, exact quote, count and sample limits from the newsletter hand-back can set the goal of the next story email. The story run still needs the org context (required), one true story from the owner, the list and the one action, and exported numbers after sending.

tools/orchestrator-pages/price-your-soft.adaptation: Restate the product description and who pays, the tier names as variants, and the current and proposed tier prices as price today, so the survey shows every respondent the same product text.
tools/orchestrator-pages/price-your-soft.output_quote: The value metric (what you charge for that grows with the customer's value), the good, better, best tier layout and the starting price for each.
tools/orchestrator-pages/price-your-soft.input_quote: **Your product facts and what it does for buyers** (required): price today, variants, what it is made of, how it is used and the problem it solves.
tools/orchestrator-pages/price-your-soft.rationale: The tier plan suggests checking the tiers with buyers first. Its product description, tiers and starting prices pass as the product facts the willingness-to-pay survey is built on. The next workflow still needs people to survey, a 90-day sales export and per-product costs from the person's own books; the handoff does not create these, and its store-style cost inputs fit software only loosely.

catalogue-items/orchestrators/stress-tes.output_quote: case.pptx, or the slide-by-slide outline if the file could not be built (say which)
catalogue-items/orchestrators/stress-tes.input_quote: The team's recommendation and current deck (or its text).
catalogue-items/orchestrators/stress-tes.rationale: The revised deck from the stress test is the current deck the review assistant checks and rebuilds where changes touch it. It still needs the full case, exhibits, rubric and time limit, and nothing is submitted without a clear yes.

catalogue-items/orchestrators/turn-a-des.adaptation: Turn the planned tasks and who uses the screen into a research question about the changed screen, with the tasks marked as a draft for the user to confirm.
catalogue-items/orchestrators/turn-a-des.output_quote: Write three to five tasks to check the changes, in plain words and with no hints on where to click.
catalogue-items/orchestrators/turn-a-des.input_quote: The research question, the type and number of users and the 3 to 5 tasks.
catalogue-items/orchestrators/turn-a-des.rationale: The test plan's tasks and audience give the research question and draft tasks; the revised prototype itself must still be made and supplied, and participants and consent are not created.

catalogue-items/orchestrators/turn-rough.adaptation: Paste the EDITED TEXT section, with the original rough notes if available, as the session material in full. State the skill and the moment of use separately; do not pass the .docx or PDF file paths as the material.
catalogue-items/orchestrators/turn-rough.output_quote: Pass to step 2: the edited text with the note behind each claim.
catalogue-items/orchestrators/turn-rough.input_quote: **The material** (required): slides, notes or a transcript from the session.
catalogue-items/orchestrators/turn-rough.rationale: The plain-English edited handout text, traced to the notes, passes as the session material for a one-page desk version. The handout writer still needs the skill in one line and when it is used, and it works only if the notes hold fixed steps.

tools/orchestrator-pages/win-a-deal-agai.adaptation: State the talk from the action plan: the buyer meeting, the signature date as the deadline and the step wanted from them, and add the buyer's objection words as what they said last time.
tools/orchestrator-pages/win-a-deal-agai.output_quote: Then work backwards from the signature date: every step with an owner on either side and a date.
tools/orchestrator-pages/win-a-deal-agai.input_quote: **The talk** (required): who you are meeting, what you want from them, your deadline, and what you could give.
tools/orchestrator-pages/win-a-deal-agai.rationale: The mutual action plan passes the buyer, the signature date and the open steps, and the objection replies give the buyer's past words. The prep planner still needs the walk-away point and what the person could give, which only the person knows.

tools/orchestrator-pages/write-design-ru.adaptation: Take one screen's layout, components, states and edge cases from the developer spec and write them as the 'clear description' of that single screen for the usability reviewer, naming the tokens it uses.
tools/orchestrator-pages/write-design-ru.output_quote: Give it the rule sheet, the token file and any screens or mock-ups the person has.
tools/orchestrator-pages/write-design-ru.input_quote: **One screen or prototype** (required): a screenshot, a Figma link or a clear description.
tools/orchestrator-pages/write-design-ru.rationale: One screen's spec passes as a described screen to review before build. The review still needs who uses it and their task. A screenshot of the built screen is better evidence, and the review is expert-style: no user test has been run.
tools/orchestrator-pages/write-design-ru.condition: Only when the person gave screens or mock-ups to step 4, so the spec describes a real screen; a spec built only from rules and tokens has no screen to review.

catalogue-items/ecommerce/amazon-launch-.adaptation: Copy the normal price and the units in stock from the launch plan into the keeper's first product facts sheet. The owner adds landed cost, size, weight and category, and the month's fee, sales and stock reports from Seller Central.
catalogue-items/ecommerce/amazon-launch-.output_quote: Launch price: <...>   Normal price: <...>   Limit: <first n units>
catalogue-items/ecommerce/amazon-launch-.input_quote: **Product facts** (required the first time): price, landed cost, size and weight of the packed unit, category.
catalogue-items/ecommerce/amazon-launch-.rationale: After launch, the plan's price and stock check seed the keeper's first product facts. The keeper still needs the month's own reports, which the plan cannot give.

catalogue-items/ecommerce/store-name-gen.output_quote: NEXT: run the shortlist through the Store name tester.
catalogue-items/ecommerce/store-name-gen.input_quote: Paste your own shortlist, or make one first with the [Store name generator]
catalogue-items/ecommerce/store-name-gen.rationale: The generator's shortlist of names is what the tester scores. The owner picks two to five of the ten to fifteen names, and the tester still asks what is sold and who buys it.

catalogue-items/general/creative-ai-chat.adaptation: Paste the tailored prompt into a chat AI, then bring the draft it writes to the voice editor as numbered lines. The prompt itself is not edited for voice.
catalogue-items/general/creative-ai-chat.output_quote: Add a line that the prompt produces a draft.
catalogue-items/general/creative-ai-chat.input_quote: Any other copy draft, such as an email with its subject and preview lines, works too when given as numbered lines.
catalogue-items/general/creative-ai-chat.rationale: The prompt makes a first draft, and that draft is what the voice editor checks against the org context's voice rules.

catalogue-items/general/launch-task-forc.output_quote: Cover in order: the job in one sentence, the buyer, the launch date and key limits
catalogue-items/general/launch-task-forc.input_quote: **What is in the launch scope** (required): the smaller list, so no stage shows a cut feature.
catalogue-items/general/launch-task-forc.rationale: Once the product is built, the kickoff plan's job, launch date and limits carry into the teaser planner. The planner still needs the final scope list, and it marks the scope missing if the plan does not list it.

catalogue-items/general/power-and-fear-m.adaptation: Take the map's wants, fears and help, block or hurt lines for the person you are meeting and paste them as what you know about them, next to the talk details the user still gives.
catalogue-items/general/power-and-fear-m.output_quote: A want is what they are trying to gain. A fear is what they are trying not to lose
catalogue-items/general/power-and-fear-m.input_quote: **What you know about them** (optional): their role, past words, what they said last time, what they seem to care about.
catalogue-items/general/power-and-fear-m.rationale: The map says what the other side wants and fears, which the call planner uses to prepare the talk. The user still gives the deal, the deadline and what they can offer.

catalogue-items/general/weak-position-ne.output_quote: Firm terms and what you can give.
catalogue-items/general/weak-position-ne.input_quote: A terms plan from the Negotiation prep planner for the weaker side fits here.
catalogue-items/general/weak-position-ne.rationale: The weaker side's terms plan gives the firm terms and what can be given, which the call planner reads as the user's limits. The user still describes the talk itself.

catalogue-items/imported/partner-campaig.adaptation: Name the partner picked in the campaign plan and the asks in its pitch as the question for the evaluator: what tier to sign them at. The user fills the intake facts, such as named accounts and sales team size, from the partner.
catalogue-items/imported/partner-campaig.output_quote: Pick one partner and write one campaign plan
catalogue-items/imported/partner-campaig.input_quote: At what tier should we sign them?
catalogue-items/imported/partner-campaig.rationale: After a campaign is planned with one partner, the evaluator checks whether that partner is real and what terms fit. The plan names the partner; the intake facts must come from the partner.

tools/orchestrator-pages/write-a-clear-e.adaptation: Paste the final subject and reply text from the hand-back as the draft. Keep the facts checked list beside it so the editor leaves those facts as they are.
tools/orchestrator-pages/write-a-clear-e.output_quote: SUBJECT AND REPLY (final, after the voice edit)
tools/orchestrator-pages/write-a-clear-e.input_quote: **Your draft** (required): the text as it is.
tools/orchestrator-pages/write-a-clear-e.rationale: The finished reply is a short text the plain English editor can make easier to read. It is a draft email, not a procedure or report, so it goes in as the draft.
